exercises.instruction: Choose the correct quantifier. There are exactly two candidates.
exercises.prompt: ___ candidates were highly qualified for the position.
exercises.explanation: 'Both' = exactly two. 'All' would imply more than two. 'Both candidates' → plural verb 'were'.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct verb form.
exercises.prompt: Each participant ___ required to submit a signed consent form.
exercises.explanation: 'Each' + singular noun → singular verb. 'Each participant is required...'

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct quantifier. You want to emphasise individual attention.
exercises.prompt: The teacher gave ___ student detailed feedback on their essay.
exercises.explanation: 'Each' emphasises individual distribution — giving one copy/feedback to every individual one by one.

exercises.instruction: Identify the grammatical error.
options: All the students passed the final exam.
Both reports were submitted on time.
Every of the participants received a certificate.
Each team member contributed to the project.
exercises.answer: Every of the participants received a certificate.
exercises.explanation: 'Every' cannot be followed by 'of'. Use 'Every participant received...' or 'Each of the participants received...'.

exercises.instruction: Identify the verb agreement error.
options: All the documents were reviewed by the committee.
Both the managers approved the plan.
Each student are expected to bring their own materials.
Every country has its own legal system.
exercises.answer: Each student are expected to bring their own materials.
exercises.explanation: 'Each' + singular noun → singular verb. 'Each student **is** expected to bring their own materials.'

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct structure with 'each of'.
exercises.prompt: ___ the applicants will be interviewed individually.
exercises.explanation: 'Each of' must be followed by 'the' + plural noun: 'Each of the applicants'. 'Every of' is not grammatical.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct quantifier for a universal statement about a large group.
exercises.prompt: ___ country in the world has its own currency.
exercises.explanation: 'Every' = universal (no exceptions), typically for larger groups. 'Every country has' — singular verb.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct mid-position structure.
exercises.prompt: The students ___ completed the survey before the deadline.
exercises.explanation: 'All' can appear in mid-position after a subject: 'The students all completed' (= all the students completed).

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct quantifier. The buses run at a fixed interval.
exercises.explanation: 'Every + number + plural noun' = at regular intervals: 'every fifteen minutes', 'every three days'.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: 'all', 'both', 'each', or 'every'.
exercises.prompt: ___ member of the team was asked to present their results.
exercises.explanation: 'Each member' (individual focus) or 'Every member' (universal) — both correct here. Singular verb 'was'.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: 'all' or 'both'. There are exactly two options.
exercises.explanation: Exactly two options → 'Both'. 'All' implies more than two.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: the correct verb form for 'every'.
exercises.prompt: Every employee ___ required to complete annual training.
exercises.explanation: 'Every' + singular noun → singular verb: 'Every employee is required'.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: 'each of the' or 'every'. The sentence needs 'each of the'.
exercises.prompt: ___ students submitted a different version of the project.
exercises.explanation: 'Each of the' + plural noun. 'Every student' would also work but 'Each of the students' is the target structure.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct answer for: the correct pronoun position. They = the two managers.
exercises.prompt: The two managers ___ agreed to sign the contract.
exercises.explanation: 'They both agreed' or 'The two managers both agreed' — 'both' appears after the subject pronoun/noun.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Setiap negara memiliki budaya dan tradisinya sendiri."
exercises.prompt: Setiap negara memiliki budaya dan tradisinya sendiri.
options: traditions. and culture own its has country Every
Every country has its own culture and traditions.
Every country has is iting own culture and is traditioning.
Every country have its own culture and traditions.
exercises.answer: Every country has its own culture and traditions.
exercises.explanation: 'Setiap' = every (universal). Singular noun + singular verb: 'every country has'.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Kedua proposal tersebut ditolak oleh komite."
exercises.prompt: Kedua proposal tersebut ditolak oleh komite.
options: Both proposals are rejected by the committee.
Both proposals were rejected by the committee.
Both proposals were rejected by a committee.
Both is proposaling were rejected by the committee.
exercises.answer: Both proposals were rejected by the committee.
exercises.explanation: 'Keduanya' = both (exactly two). Plural noun → plural verb 'were'.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Guru tersebut memberikan umpan balik kepada setiap siswa secara individual."
exercises.prompt: Guru tersebut memberikan umpan balik kepada setiap siswa secara individual.
options: The teacher gave each student individual feedback. (incorrect)
The teacher gave each student individual feedback, every day.
The teacher gave each student individual feedback.
exercises.answer: The teacher gave each student individual feedback.
exercises.explanation: 'Setiap siswa' with individual distribution → 'each student'. Singular noun, singular implied verb.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English: "Semua dokumen harus dikumpulkan sebelum tenggat waktu."
exercises.prompt: Semua dokumen harus dikumpulkan sebelum tenggat waktu.
options: All documents must be submitted before the deadline. (incorrect)
All documents must be submitted before the deadline, every day.
All documents must be submitted before the deadline.
All documents must be submitted before a deadline.
exercises.answer: All documents must be submitted before the deadline.
exercises.explanation: 'Semua' = all. Plural noun → plural verb implied. 'All documents' (no article) or 'all the documents' (specific).

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct fixed expression.
exercises.prompt: They helped ___ other throughout the difficult project.
exercises.explanation: 'Each other' is a fixed expression meaning mutual action. 'Every other' means 'alternate'.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: She worked ___ day without taking a break.
exercises.explanation: 'The whole day' = the entire day (singular). 'All day' is also correct (fixed expression) — but 'all the day' is not natural. 'The whole day' is the best option here.
